comparison: Both evaluate RDKit-based conformer sampling methodology (C8, C9, C25, C26). OpenEval finds the implementation well-documented and supported by strain reduction data. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as a 'clear and systematic description' of methodological improvements, with full agreement on this capability.

Both address development dataset performance metrics (C12, C13, C27-C29, C48-C52). OpenEval finds quantitative results well-documented and supported. Peer reviewers accept the improvements but characterize them as 'modest' rather than transformative, representing a difference in emphasis rather than disagreement on factual claims.

OpenEval R3 addresses comparative performance against prior version (C14, C15, C53-C56). Peer R2 includes some of these claims (C14, C15, C53-C55) in their evaluation of overall performance improvements, also characterizing them as modest but supported.

Both evaluate operational bounds from synthetic dataset (C58, C59). OpenEval finds the synthetic dataset approach provides appropriate evidence for these bounds. Peer reviewer expresses significant concern that synthetic data may be optimistic and 'the resolution cutoff will be even stricter when applied to real-world data,' representing substantive disagreement on generalizability.

Both address unbiased validation dataset results (C60-C65). OpenEval finds the independent validation strengthens confidence in generalizability. Peer reviewers accept these results without challenge as part of 'solid evidence of improved capabilities through careful validation,' showing full agreement.

Both evaluate high-strain dataset results (C67-C70). OpenEval finds the demonstration of strain reduction in single-conformer models appropriate. Peer reviewers do not challenge these results and implicitly accept them as supporting 'modest improvements in the strain of the proposed conformers,' showing agreement.

Both address macrocycle modeling capability (C74-C77). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to 51% attrition rate raising selection bias concerns. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as a capability expansion ('allowing for multi conformer modeling of macrocyclic compounds') without emphasizing the high failure rate, representing different emphasis on the same data.

Both evaluate fragment screening results (C10, C80-C86). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to mixed results and ~33% complete failures. Peer reviewers do not explicitly discuss fragment results but raise related concerns about 'sensitivity to initial ligand placement' with 'ambiguous cases,' showing implicit alignment with OpenEval's uncertainty.

Both address cryo-EM extension (C11, C87-C91). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to extremely small sample size (n=4) limiting generalizability. Peer reviewers acknowledge the extension without challenge, accepting it as part of expanded capabilities, representing different standards for what constitutes adequate proof-of-principle.

Both evaluate limitations regarding large conformational changes (C92-C94). OpenEval finds these limitations accurately described and appropriately acknowledged. Peer reviewer explicitly raises the same concern about 'sensitivity to initial ligand placement' with 'ambiguous cases,' showing full agreement on this limitation.

Both address macrocycle refinement infrastructure limitations (C95, C96, and related C71-C73). OpenEval finds the acknowledgment appropriate and supported by quantitative attrition data. Peer reviewers do not challenge these technical difficulties, implicitly accepting them as part of ongoing field-wide challenges, showing agreement.

Both evaluate computational performance metrics (C41-C43). OpenEval finds the performance characteristics well-documented with appropriate statistical measures. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these details as part of 'thorough analysis,' showing agreement without explicit discussion.

OpenEval evaluates dataset curation process (C44-C47) as supported with clear filtering steps and quality control. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not explicitly discuss data curation methodology.

OpenEval evaluates methodological constraints on conformer numbers (C38-C39) as supported design choices. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not discuss these specific algorithmic limits.
OpenEval evaluates RSCC interpretation standards (C57) as appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not discuss metric interpretation standards.

OpenEval evaluates scientific context and motivation (C1-C5) as supported by established knowledge and citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not explicitly evaluate background claims.

OpenEval evaluates prior version limitations (C6, C7, C23, C24) as supported by citations and comparative data. Peer R5 touches on C7 regarding macrocycle limitations but does not comprehensively evaluate these historical context claims.

OpenEval evaluates methodological extensions context (C10, C11, C33-C36) as supported by experimental demonstrations and citations. Peer reviewers acknowledge the extensions (R6, R7) but do not evaluate the contextual claims about growth in fragment screening and cryo-EM methods.

OpenEval evaluates scientific rationale for multiconformer modeling (C16-C21) as supported by established knowledge and citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not explicitly evaluate these foundational claims.

OpenEval evaluates core algorithmic approach description (C22) as properly cited and detailed. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not explicitly evaluate this methodological description claim.

OpenEval evaluates macrocycle context and properties (C30-C32) as well-cited and supported. Peer R5 touches on C32 regarding prior approach difficulties but does not comprehensively evaluate these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates strain metric context (C66) as appropriately cited with meaningful rationale. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not discuss the strain threshold justification.
